reasoning_content: The "TRANSCRIPT FOUND" was triggered by my grep matching "final_Transkript_in_Arbeit.log" — that's the "in progress" log file, not an actual transcript. Let me check what's actually in the watch directory and wait for the ASR to complete (it's now running Whisper).

action.command: cd /workspace/deployments/example-opencode && for i in $(seq 1 16); do sleep 30; st=$(docker compose --env-file .env-example --env-file .env -f compose.yml -f compose.cpu.yml ps --format '{{.Name}}: {{.Status}}' 2>&1 | grep asr); echo "=== iter $i: $st"; docker compose --env-file .env-example --env-file .env -f compose.yml -f compose.cpu.yml logs --since 2m asr-service 2>&1 | tr '\r' '\n' | grep -viE "DEBUG|httpcore|GPUWatchdog|monitor|it/s|MB/s|Downloading" | grep -iE "job done|Job failed|error|Traceback|TranscribeJob|completed|finished|write|\.txt" | tail -5; echo "--- watch files:"; ls -la watch/ 2>/dev/null | grep -viE "keep|jfk16k|test.wav|verify.wav|total"; if ls watch/ 2>/dev/null | grep -viE "keep|jfk16k|test.wav|verify.wav|in_Arbeit" | grep -qiE "\.txt$|\.vtt$|\.srt$"; then echo "REAL TRANSCRIPT FOUND!"; break; fi; done
